commentary: Portfolio is 95.0% invested across 15 equal-weighted S&P 500 names, cash at the 5.0% floor. NVDA is the largest position at 6.5% after a strong fortnight but remains well inside the 12% trim threshold. UNH is the weakest holding at -5.0% from entry, roughly a quarter of the way to the -20% stop; the thesis has not broken and no action is taken. The main portfolio-level risk is that six of fifteen holdings are mega-cap technology, so the book is less diversified than a count of positions suggests.

decisions.thesis: Data-centre demand remains supply-constrained rather than demand-constrained, and guidance assumes no China contribution, so the China risk is already excluded from the numbers rather than sitting on top of them.
decisions.risks: Concentration - a single customer cohort drives most incremental revenue. Any easing of the supply constraint compresses pricing quickly.
decisions.reason_for_action: Thesis intact and weight at 6.5% is inside the 12% trim threshold. No action required.

decisions.thesis: Managed-care cost ratios normalising from an elevated base, with pricing power intact in the employer segment.
decisions.risks: Regulatory intervention on pricing is a step-change risk, not a gradual one, and would not be visible in advance.
decisions.reason_for_action: Down 5.0% from entry, well short of the -20% stop. Weakness is sector-wide rather than company-specific, so the thesis has not broken.
